value.body: Degrees in physical education and sport. You study anatomy, physiology, sports training, coaching of particular sports, yoga, and teaching methods, with a large share of time on the field. After Class 12 the main options are a three-year B.P.E.S. / B.P.E. or a four-year B.P.Ed at some institutes; the better-known two-year B.P.Ed is a teacher-training course taken after a first degree.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 3-year B.P.E.S. / B.P.E.; 4-year B.P.Ed after Class 12 at some institutes; the 2-year B.P.Ed comes after a degree

items.label: Regulator for teacher-training versions
items.note: B.P.Ed and M.P.Ed need NCTE recognition

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 pass, usually with a minimum aggregate. Most institutes add a physical fitness test and a sports skill test to a written test; some central institutes use CUET-UG for the written part. Sports achievements often count in the merit list, and some institutes set an upper age limit.

value.title: At a glance
items: Teaching physical education in schools usually needs the B.P.Ed, not only a B.P.E.S.
Coaching jobs depend heavily on your own sport and coaching certifications.
Fitness and sports-business jobs are mostly private and vary in pay and stability.
Check NCTE recognition before joining any B.P.Ed or M.P.Ed course.
